2026-02-21.notes: What about energy? We can say energy moves from place to place and since it's not destroyed, it has life? That's a really interesting way to think about it.
What about the stars? They have life cycles, are 'born,' but also die at the end of their life cycle. Does that make them alive?
Stars have lifecycles. Sun is a star. If stars are alive, then the sun is alive? That doesn't feel right but I can't explain why.
Sun is nonliving but gives life. A rocking horse is nonliving but doesn't give life. So there are different kinds of nonliving things!
Living things must grow and reproduce. The sun doesn't reproduce, so it's definitely not alive by that definition.
The sun changes over time, but not in the same way organisms do. It doesn't respond to stimuli or maintain homeostasis.
If we said everything that provides energy for life is alive, then we'd have to say food is alive too. That breaks the whole definition.
